title: Determine if a Simple Graph Exists
summary: Given an integer array where each element represents the desired degree of the corresponding vertex, determine if it is possible to form an undirected simple graph with these degrees, ensuring that there are no self-loops or parallel edges between the same pair of vertices.
statement: Given an integer array where each element represents the desired degree of the corresponding vertex, determine if it is possible to form an undirected simple graph with these degrees, ensuring that there are no self-loops or parallel edges between the same pair of vertices. Return true if such a graph can be formed, otherwise return false.
constraints: One to 100,000 requested degrees, each from zero to n-1.
The graph must be undirected and simple: no loops or parallel edges.
Return whether exactly this degree sequence is realizable.
reference_solution:
def simple_graph_exists(degrees):
    import bisect
    n=len(degrees);values=sorted(degrees,reverse=True)
    if any(value<0 or value>=n for value in values) or sum(values)%2:return False
    prefix=[0]
    for value in values:prefix.append(prefix[-1]+value)
    negative=[-value for value in values]
    for count in range(1,n+1):
        split=bisect.bisect_left(negative,-count,count)
        available=count*(count-1)+(split-count)*count+prefix[n]-prefix[split]
        if prefix[count]>available:return False
    return True

hints: The Erdős-Gallai inequalities characterize graphical degree sequences.
Sort degrees downward and use prefix sums plus binary search to evaluate each inequality quickly.
Check even total degree, then compare every top-k demand with its maximum possible internal and suffix connections.
The handshake lemma supplies parity, and satisfying all Erdős-Gallai inequalities is necessary and sufficient for a simple graph.
